canonical_claim: Let (X_k)_{k=0}^n be a real-valued martingale adapted to a filtration. If deterministic nonnegative constants c_k satisfy |X_k - X_{k-1}| <= c_k almost surely for k=1,...,n, then for every t >= 0, P(X_n - X_0 >= t) <= exp(-t^2 / (2 * sum_{k=1}^n c_k^2)); the corresponding lower-tail bound follows by negation, and their union gives the two-sided bound with factor 2.
